passage:
A clinic introduced a digital queue system. Patients could check their waiting number on a screen or phone.
The system reduced crowding, but some patients still waited anxiously. Numbers moved slowly, and no one knew why.
The clinic added updates: emergency cases, doctor breaks, and estimated waiting times. Patients became calmer when they understood the delay.
The clinic learned that information is part of care. People can wait better when they are not left guessing.
A queue is not only a line of numbers. It is a line of people with worries, schedules, and pain. Good systems respect that.
